runtime: current checkout source via explicit aliases; no package dist from other checkout
preparation: PR 3208 host.ts copy with import targets, phase marks and mounted-render paint completion instrumentation
formal: Untraced. No forced eager compile hint or engine flag. Two identical fetch arms plus factory arm. 3 trials x 20 rounds x 2 workloads x 2 CPU profiles; 2 warmups per arm per cell. No post-hoc removal or threshold changes.
trace: Separate Chrome process per workload/arm, V8 function event logging plus CDP Tracing. Timings in these traces are diagnostic only. Nested event durations must not be summed as exclusive CPU time.
limitations: Representative application fixtures using real published dependencies, not a deployed business application
One machine and Chromium; CPU throttle is not a physical slow device
Ready state deliberately tests complete preparation; does not establish hit rate
HTTP resources use fixed 20ms latency with no bandwidth throttle
Host workload is synthetic 30ms; fixed input at 50ms does not validate all interaction phases
Heap is sampled JS heap and includes preparation caches before release; not stable RSS

validatedOutcome.recommendation: Continue the opt-in classic preparation investigation; demonstrated hit-case activation improvement, not sufficient evidence for default scheduling or public API rollout.
